message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.26","text":"But the one among the sons of humanity who possesses prophecy, innate and proper to the soul, plainly, as a male revealing the hopes of the coming age, named his own son Abel, a name that without any doubt is interpreted “mourning.” For he causes his sons to mourn for their deceived brothers, while unfailingly promising them consolation in the coming age. He says that one should petition only one God; he neither speaks of gods himself nor believes anyone else who does. He guards whatever good he has and increases it further. He hates sacrifices, blood, and libations. He loves the chaste, the pure, and the holy. He extinguishes the fire of altars. He abolishes wars and teaches peace. He commands self-control. He does away with sins. He sanctions marriage and permits continence; he leads everyone into purity. He makes people merciful. He establishes righteousness as law, seals the perfect among them, and reveals the word of rest. He prophesies definite things and speaks clearly. He frequently reminds them of the eternal fire of punishment, continually proclaims the kingdom of God, announces heavenly wealth, promises glory that cannot be taken away, and demonstrates the forgiveness of sin by deed.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"προφητείαν ἔμφυτον ψυχῆς ἰδίαν","chosen":"prophecy, innate and proper to the soul","rationale":"Both adjectives modify “prophecy”; the genitive presents it as something distinctive or proper to the soul."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἄρσην","chosen":"as a male","rationale":"Preserves the passage’s explicit male–female contrast without replacing it with a theological title."},{"source_quote":"θεὸν ἕνα μόνον αἰτεῖν","chosen":"one should petition only one God","rationale":"The infinitive has an understood general subject, and αἰτεῖν here denotes making requests to the one God."},{"source_quote":"γάμον νομιτεύει","chosen":"sanctions marriage","rationale":"The uncommon νομιτεύει presents marriage as recognized or established as lawful."},{"source_quote":"δικαιοσύνην νομιτεύει","chosen":"establishes righteousness as law","rationale":"The same uncommon verb is retained with legal force, though idiomatic English requires a different construction from “sanctions marriage.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸν τῆς ἀναπαύσεως λόγον","chosen":"the word of rest","rationale":"Keeps λόγος as “word” and leaves open whether it denotes a message, teaching, or account concerning rest."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.27","text":"And why is there any need to say more? The male is wholly truth, the female wholly error, while the one born from male and female speaks falsely in some things and truly in others. For the female, enclosing the male’s white seed in her own blood as in red fire, gives structure to what is weak in her with alien supports of bone. Giving pleasure through the flesh’s temporary bloom and secretly stealing away the strength of reason through brief pleasures, she leads most people into adultery and thus deprives them of the good bridegroom who is to come. For every human being is a bride whenever, being sown with the true prophet’s white word of truth, that person is enlightened in mind.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὁ ἄρσην ὅλος ἀλήθεια, ἡ θήλεια ὅλη πλάνη","chosen":"The male is wholly truth, the female wholly error","rationale":"Preserves the author’s stark gendered claim; πλάνη can also mean deception or wandering, but “error” fits the contrast with truth."},{"source_quote":"ἀλλοτρίοις ἐρείσμασιν ὀστέων","chosen":"with alien supports of bone","rationale":"ἀλλοτρίοις means foreign or belonging to another, while ἐρείσμασιν retains the structural image of supports."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ λογισμοῦ τὴν ἰσχὺν ὑποσυλῶσα","chosen":"secretly stealing away the strength of reason","rationale":"ὑποσυλάω conveys covert deprivation, and λογισμός here is the faculty of reasoning rather than a particular calculation."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ μέλλοντος καλοῦ στερίσκει νυμφίου","chosen":"deprives them of the good bridegroom who is to come","rationale":"The genitive depends on the verb of deprivation; μέλλοντος may also be rendered “future.”"},{"source_quote":"ὁ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος","chosen":"every human being","rationale":"The expression can formally suggest “the whole human being,” but the distributive sense fits the ensuing general condition."},{"source_quote":"φωτίζηται τὸν νοῦν","chosen":"is enlightened in mind","rationale":"The accusative marks the respect in which the person is enlightened."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.28","text":"Therefore one must listen to the one and only prophet of truth, knowing that the word sown by someone else, having incurred a charge of adultery, is cast out of his kingdom as though by a bridegroom. But for those who know the mystery, even death results from adultery of the soul. Whenever the soul is sown by others, then, as one who has acted as a prostitute or committed adultery, she is abandoned by the spirit. Thus the ensouled body, after the life-giving spirit has separated, is dissolved into earth, and at the time of judgment the punishment proportionate to the sin is rendered to the soul after the dissolution of the body—just as among human beings a woman caught in adultery is first expelled from the household and then later judged for condemnation.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὁ παρ’ ἑτέρου σπαρεὶς λόγος","chosen":"the word sown by someone else","rationale":"Preserves λόγος as the grammatical subject and the sowing metaphor, rather than substituting the person who receives the teaching."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ὑπὸ νυμφίου τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ ἐκβάλλεται","chosen":"is cast out of his kingdom as though by a bridegroom","rationale":"The rendering preserves the source’s attachment and referential ambiguity: αὐτοῦ may refer to the bridegroom, the true prophet, or another implied male authority."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ ψυχικῆς μοιχείας","chosen":"from adultery of the soul","rationale":"ψυχικός is rendered through its connection with ψυχή and the explicit soul imagery that follows; “psychic adultery” or “soulish adultery” would be more formally literal."},{"source_quote":"ὡς πορνεύσασα ἢ μοιχευσαμένη","chosen":"as one who has acted as a prostitute or committed adultery","rationale":"Distinguishes the two sexual metaphors while allowing the middle form μοιχευσαμένη its contextually defensible intransitive sense."},{"source_quote":"τὸ ἔμψυχον σῶμα","chosen":"the ensouled body","rationale":"Retains the explicit relation to ψυχή rather than reducing the phrase to the less specific “living body.”"},{"source_quote":"ἡ κατ’ ἀξίαν κόλασις","chosen":"the punishment proportionate to the sin","rationale":"κατ’ ἀξίαν denotes punishment corresponding to what is deserved."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἡ ἐπὶ μοιχείᾳ. φωραθεῖσα","issue":"The printed full stop separates the article and prepositional phrase from the participle they naturally construe with. The translation reads the words as one continuous noun phrase while acknowledging the selected edition’s confirmed punctuation.","proposed_reading":"ἡ ἐπὶ μοιχείᾳ φωραθεῖσα","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.29","text":"While Peter was about to reveal this very mystical discourse fully to us, Zacchaeus arrived and said, “Now then, Peter, it is time for you to go out and hold the discussion. For a large crowd has gathered in the courtyard and is waiting for you. In its midst Simon stands like a general, attended by it as his bodyguard.” When Peter heard this, he told me to withdraw for the sake of the prayer, since I had not yet received the baptism that leads to salvation. Then he said to those who were already perfect, “Rise, and let us pray that God, in his unfailing acts of compassion, may work with me as I press toward the salvation of the human beings created by him.” After saying this and praying, he went out into the large open-air area of the courtyard, where many had assembled in order to observe. His delay had made them all the more eager to hurry to hear him.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸν μυστικὸν λόγον","chosen":"the mystical discourse","rationale":"λόγος here denotes the esoteric explanation Peter was giving; “mystical teaching” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὸ ἐκβάντα διαλεχθῆναί σε","chosen":"for you to go out and hold the discussion","rationale":"διαλέγεσθαι may mean converse, debate, or deliver an address; “hold the discussion” leaves the precise format open."},{"source_quote":"ὡς πολέμαρχος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ δορυφορούμενος","chosen":"like a general, attended by it as his bodyguard","rationale":"The singular pronoun refers to the crowd, while δορυφορεῖν literally evokes being attended by spear-bearers and conventionally means receiving an armed escort."},{"source_quote":"τὸ πρὸς σωτηρίαν βάπτισμα","chosen":"the baptism that leads to salvation","rationale":"πρός expresses orientation or purpose; “baptism for salvation” is a more formally compact alternative."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἤδη τελείοις","chosen":"those who were already perfect","rationale":"τελείοις may contextually designate those already initiated or baptized, but the main text retains the source’s language of completion or perfection."},{"source_quote":"τῆς διακρίσεως αὐτοῦ","chosen":"his delay","rationale":"διάκρισις can denote separation, distinction, hesitation, or delay; the crowd’s increased eagerness supports “delay” here."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τὸ σπεύδειν τοῦ ἀκούειν","chosen":"to hurry to hear him","rationale":"The nested infinitives express eagerness directed toward hastening in order to listen."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.30","text":"So he stood and saw all the people gazing at him in deep silence, with Simon the magician standing in their midst, and began to speak as follows: “Peace be to all of you who stand ready to extend your right hands to the truth of God. This peace is his great and incomparable gift in the present world. The one who sent us, being an unerring prophet concerning what is supremely beneficial, commanded us to pronounce it to you in the form of a greeting before the words of instruction, so that, if anyone among you is a child of peace, peace may take hold of him through our teaching. But if any one of you does not wish to receive it, then, after shaking from our feet as testimony the dust from the roads—which we carried through our exertions and brought to you so that you might be saved—let us depart for the houses and cities of others.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"δεξιὰς διδόναι τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀληθείᾳ","chosen":"extend your right hands to the truth of God","rationale":"The idiom depicts giving one’s right hand as a sign of agreement, pledge, or welcome; retaining the physical gesture preserves the image."},{"source_quote":"ἣν αὐτοῦ μεγάλην τε καὶ ἀσύγκριτον ἐν τῷ νῦν κόσμῳ ὑπάρχουσαν δωρεὰν","chosen":"This peace is his great and incomparable gift in the present world","rationale":"The relative pronoun can refer either to the opening “peace” or, by proximity, to “truth.” The repeated references to a greeting, a child of peace, and receiving it favor “peace.”"},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἐν ὑπεροχῇ συμφέροντος ἀψευδὴς ὑπάρχων προφήτης","chosen":"being an unerring prophet concerning what is supremely beneficial","rationale":"The genitive marks the subject matter of the prophet’s reliable proclamation; ἐν ὑπεροχῇ gives the benefit preeminent or surpassing force."},{"source_quote":"προφάσει προσηγορίας","chosen":"in the form of a greeting","rationale":"πρόφασις can mean occasion, outward form, or pretext, while προσηγορία can denote an address or salutation; the context does not require a deceptive “pretext.”"},{"source_quote":"καταλάβῃ αὐτὸν ἡ εἰρήνη","chosen":"peace may take hold of him","rationale":"καταλαμβάνειν has the force of overtaking, reaching, or taking possession of someone."},{"source_quote":"ὃν διὰ τοὺς καμάτους βαστάζαντες ἠνέγκαμεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς","chosen":"which we carried through our exertions and brought to you","rationale":"The relative pronoun refers to the road dust; διὰ τοὺς καμάτους can mean because of or through their toils."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἡμῖν-ἐνετείλατο","issue":"The selected edition prints a hyphen between the dative pronoun and the verb. It has no defensible syntactic function here and is treated as typographic or editorial punctuation rather than as part of either word.","proposed_reading":"ἡμῖν ἐνετείλατο","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
